about: The smells arm's new-vs-existing judgement: growth of an existing smell fails, and a measure travels between files only from the one base definition gone from its file. Run: mutate-on-target.py TREE jpcheck/smells.py tests/test_check_smells.py tests/mutants/jpt-new-vs-existing-on-smells.json

mutants.name: an existing smell may grow, as before
edits: grew = not new and now > before
mutants.target: a 120-line function grown to 121 fails, exit 1, saying it grew

mutants.name: growth counted only when it at least doubles
edits: grew = not new and now > before
grew = not new and now >= 2 * before
mutants.target: a complexity-15 function made 16 fails, exit 1, saying it grew

mutants.name: staying the same counted as growth
edits: grew = not new and now > before
grew = not new and now >= before
mutants.target: CONTROL: both unchanged only warn, exit 0

mutants.name: a name defined in two base files still carries a measure
mutants.target: G: a main gone from keep.py, while twin.py has one too, is not known to have moved

mutants.name: a definition still in its base file still carries its measure
edits:
if _defines(lang, now.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") if now.is_file() else None, name):
        return (0, 0, 0)
mutants.target: F: a NEW main of complexity 12 does not inherit the 20 of a main still in keep.py

mutants.name: a function that really moved is measured as new
mutants.target: E: a smelly function moved out into a new file is existing
